angle: the mechanism that makes it happen: the moving parts, the thing in the hand
subject: The mechanism as eight stone pipes standing in an arc in the surge, each cut to a partial's length, so every wave that blows across their mouths rings a chord; the stone's turned-away sides are hatched and the fundamental's mouth is the brightest edge.
controls: swell: the surge crests on the water in front of the pipes spread apart or crowd together (position).
depth: the pool stands higher round the pipes, the waterline rising up every pipe, over 24 px (position of the waterline).
salt: the pipes' heights stretch from a harmonic ladder to an inharmonic one, the short pipes getting shorter (shape of the skyline; each pipe a node scaled or pre-drawn).
drift: each pipe leans its own small way about its foot, tops wandering up to ~25 px (rotation per pipe).
reference: library/theseus-tower (cylinders in a row, outlines over black)
risks: A row of graduated cylinders can read as a bar chart or organ pipes rather than a rock pool; the arc helps but it is still close. Hatching on eight pipes is static but dense (~60 hairlines). Salt changing pipe heights needs per-pipe pre-drawn variants or scaled nodes, and scaling would thicken the hatching.
